# Generated mocks

This page shows the code the generator writes for a mocked interface. After reading it you can find the class behind a mock, see how a call reaches its setup, and see where `Setup()` and `Calls()` come from.

## Example

For `IPriceList` in `samples/Billing/Billing.cs`, named in `Mock.Of<IPriceList>()`, the generator writes this file:

<!-- snippet: GeneratedCodeSpecs.Mock_for_the_billing_sample.verified.txt -->
<a id='snippet-GeneratedCodeSpecs.Mock_for_the_billing_sample.verified.txt'></a>
```txt
// <auto-generated/>
#nullable enable
#pragma warning disable
namespace VerificationGlue.Mocks.Generated
{
    internal sealed class Billing_IPriceList_Mock : global::Billing.IPriceList, global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.IMock
    {
        private readonly global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.MockAdapter _adapter = new global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.MockAdapter("Billing_IPriceList_Mock");

        global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.MockAdapter global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.IMock.Adapter => this._adapter;

        int global::Billing.IPriceList.PriceOf(string sku)
        {
            var __args = new object?[] { sku };
            return this._adapter.Call<int>(0, "PriceOf", null, __args);
        }

        global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<int> global::Billing.IPriceList.PriceOfAsync(string sku)
        {
            var __args = new object?[] { sku };
            return this._adapter.CallTask<int>(1, "PriceOfAsync", null, __args);
        }
    }
}

namespace VerificationGlue.Mocks.Generated
{

        internal Billing_IPriceList_Setup(global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.MockAdapter adapter)
        {
            this.__adapter = adapter;
        }

        public global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.MockSetup<int> PriceOf(global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.Arg<string> sku)
            => this.__adapter.SetupCall<int>(0, "PriceOf", null, new object?[] { sku });

        public global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.MockSetup<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<int>> PriceOfAsync(global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.Arg<string> sku)
            => this.__adapter.SetupCall<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<int>>(1, "PriceOfAsync", null, new object?[] { sku });
    }

    internal sealed class Billing_IPriceList_Calls
    {
        private readonly global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.MockAdapter __adapter;

        internal Billing_IPriceList_Calls(global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.MockAdapter adapter)

        public global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.CallCount PriceOf(global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.Arg<string> sku)
```

## The mock class

The generator writes one file per mocked type, named after the type, such as `Billing_IPriceList_Mock.g.cs`. The class implements each member explicitly, so members with the same name in two inherited interfaces do not collide.

Each member packs its arguments into an array and calls its own `MockAdapter`. The adapter records the call, finds the latest setup that matches and returns its value. The `Call` method is chosen from the return type: `Call<T>`, `CallTask<T>` and so on. The adapter therefore knows the auto-value for an unconfigured call without reflection. A member that returns another mockable interface calls `CallMock<T>`, which creates the [recursive mock](../recursive-mocks.md).

The number before the member name is its ID. `Setup()` and `Calls()` pass the same ID, so both styles reach the same records.

## Setup() and Calls()

The same file holds the typed surface. `Billing_IPriceList_Setup` and `Billing_IPriceList_Calls` have one member per method and property getter, with each parameter typed `Arg<T>`. The extension methods `Setup()` and `Calls()` are in the `VerificationGlue.Mocks` namespace, so the `using` that brings in `Mock.Of<T>()` also brings them in.

## The registry

One more file registers every mock in a module initializer:

<!-- snippet: GeneratedCodeSpecs.Registry_for_the_billing_sample.verified.txt -->
<a id='snippet-GeneratedCodeSpecs.Registry_for_the_billing_sample.verified.txt'></a>
```txt
// <auto-generated/>
#nullable enable
#pragma warning disable
namespace VerificationGlue.Mocks.Generated
{
    internal static class MockRegistration
    {
        [global::System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ModuleInitializer]
        internal static void Register()
        {
            global::VerificationGlue.Mocks.MockRegistry.Register<global::Billing.IPriceList>(static () => new Billing_IPriceList_Mock());
        }
    }
}
```
<sup><a href='/test/VerificationGlue.Mocks.Generator.Specs/Snapshots/GeneratedCodeSpecs.Registry_for_the_billing_sample.verified.txt#L1-L14' title='Snippet source file'>snippet source</a> | <a href='#snippet-GeneratedCodeSpecs.Registry_for_the_billing_sample.verified.txt' title='Start of snippet'>anchor</a></sup>
<!-- endSnippet -->

`Mock.Of<T>()` reads the factory from a static generic field, and `MockRegistry.Create(Type)` reads it from a dictionary. Neither uses reflection, which is why mocks work under Native AOT.

## Where these come from

`test/VerificationGlue.Mocks.Generator.Specs/GeneratedCodeSpecs.cs` runs the generator on the sample and compares the output with the snapshots shown here. A change to the generated code fails that spec until the snapshots are accepted, and this page shows the accepted snapshots.
